texts.text: 1. The performance marketing team drove the supply strategy

texts.orig: 2. The performance marketing team was only two people, even past $100m/year spend
texts.text: 2. The performance marketing team was only two people, even past $100m/year spend

texts.label: text
texts.orig: “It was actually only two guys: one banker and one coder.
texts.text: “It was actually only two guys: one banker and one coder.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Peter (the banker) was extremely competitive. He would scream and shout when he was losing his #1 position. He had a simple success criteria: win the auction for all of the important words, and make money on it.
texts.text: Peter (the banker) was extremely competitive. He would scream and shout when he was losing his #1 position. He had a simple success criteria: win the auction for all of the important words, and make money on it.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The coder was very experienced, entrepreneurial, creative and a data geek. With another coder the magic wouldn't have happened. It was the combination of Peter with the coder having excellent data skills (i.e. he built tools for supply to align with the paid search team) that made it work in the beginning.
texts.text: The coder was very experienced, entrepreneurial, creative and a data geek. With another coder the magic wouldn't have happened. It was the combination of Peter with the coder having excellent data skills (i.e. he built tools for supply to align with the paid search team) that made it work in the beginning.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Critical to getting this Product-Market Fit right was our obsession with conversion improvements and A/B testing. Each A/B test that increased bookings, or monetization, increased the performance of marketing campaigns. Conversion improvements made unviable campaigns viable, improved competitiveness of existing campaigns, and further improved ROI on campaigns where we already were #1 — allowing us to invest those margins in new frontiers for the business.
texts.text: Critical to getting this Product-Market Fit right was our obsession with conversion improvements and A/B testing. Each A/B test that increased bookings, or monetization, increased the performance of marketing campaigns. Conversion improvements made unviable campaigns viable, improved competitiveness of existing campaigns, and further improved ROI on campaigns where we already were #1 — allowing us to invest those margins in new frontiers for the business.
